title: To restore the ability of the people of American Samoa to approve amendments to the territorial constitution based on majority rule in a democratic act of self-determination, as authorized pursuant to an Act of Congress delegating administration of Federal territorial law in the territory to the President, and to the Secretary of the Interior under Executive Order 10264, dated June 29, 1951, under which the Constitution of American Samoa was approved and may be amended without requirement for further congressional action, subject to the authority of Congress under the Territorial Clause in article IV, section 3, clause 2 of the United States Constitution.
sponsor: Del. Radewagen, Aumua Amata Coleman [R-AS-At Large]
official_summary: This act repeals the statute that prevents the people of American Samoa from approving amendments or modifications to the constitution of that territory. Under that statute, an act of Congress is required for such an amendment or modification.

summary.headline: New law lets American Samoa amend its own territorial constitution by majority vote without needing a separate act of Congress.
summary.what_it_does: This law repeals an earlier federal rule that required an act of Congress before any change to American Samoa's constitution could take effect. With that rule gone, the people of American Samoa can approve changes to their constitution through their own process. Congress still keeps its overall power over US territories under the US Constitution.

who_it_affects.group: Residents and voters of American Samoa
who_it_affects.how: They can approve changes to their territorial constitution by majority vote without waiting for Congress to pass a law.
Constitutional changes it proposes no longer need separate congressional approval to take effect.
The Secretary keeps a role in overseeing American Samoa's constitution under a 1951 executive order, now without the extra step of congressional action.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 4, 2025; no separate effective date is given in the summary.
